title: Tangential link to pitch plate -- grip length, take 2

joint.description: Same joint as tan_link_to_pitch_plate. The workbook's second pass reorganises the flanged bushing into one sub-total and drops the separate washer/pitch-plate branch.

provenance.relationship: Take 2's total (E49) is arithmetically identical to take 1's bore_min_grip (E18) -- same nominal 20.485, same LMC 19.9218, same MMC 20.7368. It is a restatement, not a revision.

elements.name: flange bushing flange thickness
elements.note: Workbook comment on this row: 'does not include chamfer' -- the chamfer is a separate subtracted element below.

source_ref.note: Take 2 evaluates only the -13; the -14 branch was dropped.

elements.name: nut minor diameter (.19-32 UNJF)
elements.note: UNUSED by any path or check in the workbook. An internal feature, so MMC is the SMALLEST hole (4.05) -- the workbook has this the right way round. No nominal was given; 4.15 here is the midpoint, supplied by transcription.

elements.name: nut c'bore diameter
elements.note: UNUSED. 0.190-0.250 in. No nominal given; 5.588 here is the midpoint, supplied by transcription.

elements.name: nut chamfer depth
elements.note: UNUSED. Derived as (c'bore dia - minor dia)/2, i.e. a 45-degree chamfer assumption. This is the start of the castellation/thread-engagement branch of the analysis; the workbook computes it and then never folds it into a check. CAUTION for any future consumer (added by review): these min/max are the workbook's column-wise pairing (LMC with LMC, MMC with MMC), not a worst-case fold of the two diameters -- a true worst case would pair max c'bore with min minor and span 0.288 to 1.15. Fold this element as-is and you understate its range.

paths.label: total bore stack (straight bushing + bearing + effective flanged bushing)

checks.label: worst case (+ = protrusion)
checks.guidance: Same quantity as take 1's threads_in_bore__13, but reported as a two-sided range rather than as a pass/fail against the minimum. Take 2 dropped the thread-transition allowance entirely, so this check is LESS conservative than take 1's on the positive side.

notes: Take 2 folds the flange thickness into the bushing sub-total (E44) instead of listing it up with the bore elements. Take 1 achieves the same by leaving cell E13 blank, so its 'total effective flange bushing L' (E16) silently excludes the flange. Both reach 20.485 -- the blank cell is a deliberate de-duplication, not an omission.
The nut_* elements are transcribed for completeness and are referenced by no path or check.
No RSS in the workbook for this stack either.
